model_annotation: This grouped bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms across six medical specialties, comparing a base model (Mistralv0.2-Base) with versions fine-tuned on each of the six specialties. The horizontal axis is labeled "Per-specialty terms" and contains six categorical groups: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis is labeled "Negative log probability" and uses a linear scale ranging from approximately -27 to -22, with tick marks at integer intervals. Each group contains seven bars representing the base model and six fine-tuned variants. The Mistralv0.2-Base model is shown in light blue, while the fine-tuned models are displayed in shades of beige to dark brown: Cardio (light beige), Gastro (light tan/peach), Infect (medium orange), Neuro (darker orange-brown), Obstetrics (dark brown), and Pediatrics (very dark brown). Since the values are negative, bars extend downward from approximately -22, with longer bars indicating more negative (lower) values. Across most specialty term groups, the Mistralv0.2-Base light blue bar tends to extend furthest downward, reaching values around -26 to -27 in the Cardio group and approximately -25 to -26 in the Neuro group, indicating the most negative log probabilities. The fine-tuned models generally show shorter bars (less negative values), clustering near -22 to -23 in many groups, such as Gastro and Obstetrics. In the Cardio group, there is notable variation among the fine-tuned models, with the Cardio fine-tuned version reaching approximately -22 while the base model extends to roughly -26.5. The Infect group shows moderate variation among fine-tuned models, with some bars reaching approximately -23.5. The Pediatrics group displays relatively uniform bar lengths across fine-tuned models, mostly near -22 to -22.5, with the base model extending to approximately -24.5. The bars within each group are not sorted by value but rather follow a consistent left-to-right ordering matching the legend sequence, and no bars appear to be visually emphasized beyond their color coding.
